Header 1x03 (J10 trigger select / J11 laser enable / J18, J19 laser output mode)

DNP: Not placed on the board - fit J10 on 2-3, J11 on 1-2 (lasers enabled), J18 and J19 on 1-2 (50 ohm outputs) by hand; keep the fifth shunt loose: J20 stays open (150 MHz) unless that Pico has passed the soak test
DNP - socket-mounted, do not place; source module separately
Mechanical only - NPTH, nothing to place

Value: U9 must be the FIXED 1.8 V NCP718 (NCP718xSN180, e.g. NCP718BSN180T1G or NCP718ASN180T1G)
Footprint: Sets the camera I/O level. The IDS UE-39B0XCP-E I/O pins are 1.8 V sensor-level; do not substitute a 1.65 V, 1.7 V or 3.3 V option.

Value: C6 is on +5V, C7 on +1V8 - use X7R, C6 rated >= 10 V
Footprint: NCP718 needs >= 1 uF ceramic on its output for stability; C7 = 2.2 uF gives margin after DC-bias derating.

Value: U12 must be a Schmitt-trigger part (74LVC1G17)
Footprint: Gives the Pixel Reset BNC TTL-compatible thresholds and 0.5-0.8 V of hysteresis at 3.3 V. A plain 74LVC1G08/1G34 is not a substitute.
Identical part and pad geometry to the stock footprints; only the silkscreen is clipped where the connector reaches the board edge. Order the standard parts.

Value: R8 is a fail-safe interlock pull-down
Footprint: Holds U10 pin 1 low when no jumper is fitted on J11, so the lasers default to DISABLED. R2 (3k3) still wins when the J11 1-2 jumper is fitted.

Value: R9 is the J10 trigger-select pull-down
Footprint: Holds PWM_TRIG_TAP (U5 input) low when no shunt is fitted on J10, so all six camera trigger lines idle low instead of floating.

Value: U7/U8/U10 must be AHCT (TTL-input) parts, not LVC
Footprint: At VCC = 5 V an LVC input needs 0.7 x VCC = 3.5 V to read high; the Pico drives these from 3.3 V GPIOs. AHCT reads high above 2.0 V.

Value: R10 = 56k sets the USB PD request to 15 V
Footprint: CH224A CFG1 table (datasheet Table 5-1): 6k8 = 9 V, 24k = 12 V, 56k = 15 V, 120k = 20 V, 210k = 28 V. Do not leave R10 off - an open CFG1 is outside the table. The laser outputs need a charger that offers 15 V (any USB-PD charger rated over 27 W).

Value: U14 must be the CH224A (not the CH224K)
Footprint: CH224A pin 1 (VHV) and pin 8 (VBUS) connect directly to VBUS_PD by copper, as the WCH CH224K-to-CH224A guide (datasheet 7.2.1) requires; R11/R15 of the CH224K design were removed. Do not fit a CH224K: it is discontinued, and its pin 1 is a 3.6 V VDD pin that VBUS_PD would destroy.

They set the 11.8 V laser-driver rail and hence the LDP-V trigger amplitude (4.54-5.14 V into 50 ohm with U13 ROH 0-8.5 ohm, window 4.5-5.2 V). With 1 % divider resistors the worst-case corners fall outside the window.

Value: U17 must be the ADJUSTABLE LT3065 (LT3065EDD), not a fixed LT3065-x
Footprint: R12/R13 (100k/5.36k) set 11.8 V from the 600 mV ADJ reference. R20 (750 ohm) sets a 400 mA current limit and C18 (22 nF) on IMAX is required by the datasheet. Solder the exposed pad (two GND vias under it).

Value: C9, C10, C17 see 12 V; C11, C12, C16 see up to 20 V
Footprint: Use >= 25 V parts for C9/C10/C17 and >= 50 V for C11/C12/C16 (X7R). C12 is the only large cap on VBUS_PD (C11 and C16 are 1 uF each): keep total VBUS capacitance near the USB-C 10 uF sink limit.

Value: U16 CE is tied to its VOUT (+5V)
Footprint: That is TI's always-on reverse-blocking connection. With CE grounded the LM66100 does NOT block reverse current.

Value: R17/R18 hold the laser pulse inputs low when the Pico is removed
Footprint: J17 can power the board with no Pico fitted; without these, U7/U8 inputs would float and an armed interlock could pass spurious laser triggers.

Value: R19 (100 ohm) isolates J10 pin 1 from the CH1 laser pulse
Footprint: With J10 on 1-2 the CH1 GPIO would otherwise also drive the ~120 mm PWM_TRIG_TAP net and arrive 0.4-1.7 ns later than CH2. Do not replace with 0 ohm.

Value: C14/C15 must keep >= 10 uF each at 5 V DC bias
Footprint: 22 uF 10 V 0805 X5R parts typically keep only 40-50 % at 5 V; 25 V-rated parts keep more. Check the chosen part's DC-bias curve.

Value: C9 (0.1 uF, 50 V) is U13's local VDD bypass
Footprint: It sits right beside U13 pin 6 with its own GND via; keep it populated and next to the driver.
An output high into 50 ohm dissipates at most 0.71 W in its resistor (1.45 W at the firmware's worst duty into a shorted BNC). Do not substitute a smaller package.

Footprint PiDG_Local:BNC_Kinghelm_KH-BNC50-3511_Horizontal: the Amphenol B6252HB-NPP3G-50 pad pattern, which the Kinghelm drawing matches within 0.04 mm (pad 1 = centre contact, pad 2 and posts = GND). 50 ohm only - never the KH-BNC75-3511. Before release, test-fit two loose parts (holes 1.0 mm pins / 2.2 mm posts, as JLC's own KH-BNC50-3511 footprint) and check shell-to-pad-2 continuity: the shell bond is one iron lead and the post housing is PBT plastic.

Value: U18 (TPS3700) is the laser power-good gate
Footprint: OUTA/OUTB hold U13 ENA/ENB low unless +12V is inside 10.6-13.3 V (R21/R22/R23 = 150k/1.2k/4.7k 1 %, worst case UV trip 10.03-10.78 V and release <= 10.89 V, OV 12.88-13.67 V; at least 0.65 V and 0.82 V outside the 11.54-12.05 V rail band). U17's own PWRGD can only sink 50 uA and is left unconnected.

Value: U3 must be a NAND (74LVC1G00); R24 (10k) pulls its gate input to +3V3
Footprint: U3 combines the J12 pixel-reset input (via U12) with the Pico gate on GP16: TDRSTN = J12 AND GATE, so either source resets the camera pixels. R24 holds the gate high (no reset) whenever the Pico is not driving it. A 74LVC1G04 here would ignore the Pico gate.

Value: J18/J19 set each laser output's mode; R25-R28 are 2 W 2512 parts
Footprint: Shunt on 1-2 = 50 ohm load (LDP-V), 4.54-5.14 V into 50 ohm. Shunt on 2-3 = Hi-Z load: 47 ohm series + 82 ohm shunt give 4.55-5.08 V open circuit from a ~50 ohm source. Worst case (output held high into a shorted BNC in Hi-Z mode) is 0.51 W in R25/R26; R27/R28 see at most 0.31 W. Do not substitute a smaller package.

Value: J20 is the clock jumper: pin 1 = CLK_SEL_JMP (through R29 1k to CLK_SEL = Pico GP10, J14 pad 14), pin 2 = GND
Footprint: Shunt fitted = 300 MHz overclock, open = the rated 150 MHz; the firmware reads it at every start with the internal pull-up (a fitted shunt reads about 0.1 V through R29). R29 limits the current to about 3.3 mA if a program drives GP10 high while the shunt is fitted (firmware before the clock jumper used GP10 as the SYNC output). Ship and leave it open unless that Pico has passed the soak test (Hardware.md, Clock jumper). Do not add a capacitor on CLK_SEL: a slow rise could read as fitted.
